executive_summary: Today's intelligence picture is defined by two converging pressures: the accelerating militarization of emerging technologies and a widening gap between the pace of threats and institutional capacity to respond. Across cyber, military, and geopolitical domains, adversaries are actively weaponizing AI, autonomous systems, and electronic warfare — from Russian anti-AI camouflage paint countering Ukrainian drone offensives, to attackers exploiting Meta's AI infrastructure, to GPS jamming threatening global aviation and shipping — while defenders are visibly struggling to keep pace, as seen in NIST's doubled vulnerability backlog, GAO criticism of Pentagon workforce cuts, and inconsistent EU critical infrastructure maturity. The undersea cable attacks and GPS disruption campaigns are particularly notable in conjunction with the South Korea nuclear submarine acceleration and Germany's military buildup, suggesting a coordinated or at minimum opportunistic exploitation of a moment of Western strategic distraction while the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire and Iran negotiations consume U.S. diplomatic bandwidth. Critical infrastructure sits at the center of this threat convergence, with the Gentlemen ransomware campaign targeting OT environments, the Oracle WebLogic exploitation, and Turkish electronic warfare capabilities all emerging simultaneously, pointing to a threat environment that is broadening faster than defensive institutions can organize against it.

sections.title: Cyber
sections.intro: Critical infrastructure vulnerabilities and AI-enabled attacks dominated cybersecurity concerns, while government agencies faced organizational challenges in vulnerability management.

items.headline: Attackers exploit Meta's AI support bot to compromise high-profile Instagram accounts
items.summary: Hackers successfully seized Instagram accounts belonging to the Obama White House and U.S. Space Force Chief Master Sergeant by manipulating Meta's AI support assistant to reset passwords. The technique spread via Telegram instructions, demonstrating how AI-powered customer service tools can become attack vectors against even high-security accounts. This represents a new class of social engineering attacks targeting automated support systems.

items.headline: NIST vulnerability database backlog doubles to 27,000 unprocessed entries
items.summary: The National Vulnerability Database's unprocessed security vulnerabilities grew from 13,000 in February 2024 to over 27,000 by end of 2025, according to an inspector general report. This massive backlog undermines the database's effectiveness as a critical resource for cybersecurity professionals and erodes public trust in government vulnerability tracking capabilities.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: CISA flags actively exploited Oracle WebLogic Server vulnerability
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2024-21182, an Oracle WebLogic Server vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. WebLogic servers are common enterprise infrastructure components, making this a significant threat to organizations running Oracle environments. Federal agencies must patch by CISA's binding operational directive deadline.

items.headline: Microsoft reverses course on legal threats against security researchers
items.summary: Microsoft clarified it has no intention to pursue legal action against individuals conducting or publishing security research, following significant backlash from the cybersecurity community. The statement comes after researchers criticized the company's perceived hostile stance toward vulnerability disclosure. This policy clarification is crucial for maintaining collaborative relationships between vendors and the security research community.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

sections.title: Geopolitical
sections.intro: Regional tensions dominate as Trump-era diplomacy reshapes Middle East dynamics while NATO faces mounting infrastructure security challenges and defense procurement pressures.

items.headline: Trump Brokers Temporary Israel-Hezbollah Ceasefire Amid Broader Iran Negotiations
items.summary: The Trump administration has secured a halt to attacks between Israel and Hezbollah as part of ongoing diplomatic efforts with Iran, though Tehran had previously suspended talks over Israeli strikes in Lebanon. A potential U.S.-Iran deal could significantly complicate Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's political position ahead of crucial upcoming elections. The diplomatic breakthrough highlights Trump's early focus on Middle East crisis management.

items.headline: Germany Accelerates Military Buildup Amid NATO Defense Spending Pressures
items.summary: Berlin is rushing to expand its rearmament efforts despite having already committed substantial resources to military modernization, facing new domestic and international obstacles. The acceleration reflects growing pressure from the Trump administration for European allies to shoulder greater defense burdens. Germany's scramble illustrates the broader challenge facing NATO members to rapidly rebuild military capabilities after decades of reduced spending.

items.headline: Critical Undersea Cable Attacks Surge Across Multiple Theaters
items.summary: NATO faces an escalating threat to critical undersea infrastructure, with multiple incidents damaging pipelines and data cables across the Baltic Sea and Red Sea regions between 2024-2025. The attacks have disrupted significant portions of Asia-Europe data traffic and highlight vulnerabilities in global communications networks. The pattern suggests coordinated efforts to target Western critical infrastructure beneath international waters.

items.headline: Global GPS Jamming Operations Threaten Commercial Aviation and Shipping
items.summary: Systematic GPS signal disruption is occurring worldwide, particularly around strategic waterways like the Strait of Hormuz and in the Baltic region, endangering civilian air and maritime traffic. The jamming appears coordinated with geopolitical tensions and represents a new front in hybrid warfare tactics. Commercial operators are struggling to maintain safe navigation as traditional backup systems prove inadequate against sophisticated electronic interference.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: Military innovation accelerates with autonomous systems reshaping Ukraine's battlefield strategy while Pentagon leadership warns allies about China's growing military capabilities.

items.headline: Ukrainian Forces Shift to Offensive Strategy Through Robotic Warfare Integration
items.summary: Ukraine's military leadership now speaks of winning rather than merely surviving, largely due to successful deployment of uncrewed and autonomous systems that have neutralized Russian numerical advantages. The rapid adaptation to robotic warfare represents a fundamental shift in battlefield dynamics. This technological evolution could reshape modern military doctrine beyond the current conflict.

items.headline: Defense Secretary Issues China Warning While Pressing Asian Allies on Military Spending
items.summary: Pentagon chief Hegseth sounded alarms over China's military buildup during discussions with Asian allies, specifically urging increased defense spending to counter Beijing's growing power. The warning reflects growing concerns about the military balance in the Pacific region. This pressure campaign suggests the U.S. is seeking to distribute defense burden-sharing beyond traditional NATO frameworks.

items.headline: South Korea Accelerates Nuclear Submarine Development Timeline
items.summary: Seoul announced plans to launch its first nuclear-powered submarine in the mid-2030s with commissioning planned for the late 2030s, marking a significant expansion of regional naval capabilities. This development adds another nuclear submarine operator in the increasingly contested Pacific theater. The timeline suggests South Korea views nuclear propulsion as essential for its strategic deterrence posture.

items.headline: GAO Criticizes Pentagon Workforce Reductions as Poorly Analyzed
items.summary: Government auditors found the Pentagon conducted workforce cuts with minimal analysis before implementation and little assessment since, raising questions about strategic planning. Defense officials acknowledged lessons should be drawn but provided no commitment to apply them. The finding highlights ongoing challenges in Pentagon management practices during a period of strategic competition.

sections.title: Intel / OSINT
sections.intro: Today's intelligence landscape features significant leadership changes at NSA, innovative countermeasures against AI-powered weapons systems, and new revelations about classified military platforms.

items.headline: NSA Names Permanent Leaders for Critical Cybersecurity Directorates
items.summary: David Imbordino has been confirmed as the new chief of NSA's cybersecurity directorate, while Bruce Jones takes command of the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center. These appointments solidify leadership continuity at the agency's most public-facing cybersecurity functions during a period of heightened threats to critical infrastructure.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: Russian Forces Deploy Anti-AI Camouflage Paint to Counter Autonomous Drones
items.summary: Russian military vehicles are now using disruptive 'dazzle' paint schemes specifically designed to confuse machine-vision targeting systems on autonomous drones. This tactical adaptation reflects the growing battlefield prevalence of AI-enabled weapons and the rapid development of countermeasures to neutralize their effectiveness.

items.headline: Turkey's HAVA SOJ Electronic Warfare Aircraft Emerges in New Satellite Imagery
items.summary: Fresh imagery reveals Turkey's previously secretive HAVA SOJ electronic warfare platform, designed to suppress enemy air defenses from standoff distances. The aircraft's public appearance suggests Turkey is advancing its indigenous electronic warfare capabilities amid regional tensions and evolving defense partnerships.

items.headline: Questions Surface About Possible U.S. MQ-1 Predator Return to Operations
items.summary: Reports of an MQ-1 drone loss to Iran have raised questions about whether the U.S. has quietly returned the officially retired Predator to active service. The incident highlights ongoing intelligence gaps about U.S. unmanned operations in contested regions and potential changes to drone deployment strategies.

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: Industrial cybersecurity consolidation accelerates as new ransomware threats target critical infrastructure while EU assessments reveal uneven security maturity across essential sectors.

items.headline: Dragos Expands Industrial Security Platform Through Phosphorus Acquisition
items.summary: Industrial cybersecurity leader Dragos acquired xIoT security firm Phosphorus to extend protection beyond traditional OT environments. The acquisition will provide enhanced asset visibility and integrated device intelligence across extended operational technology networks. This consolidation reflects the growing recognition that industrial cybersecurity must encompass broader IoT ecosystems beyond classic SCADA and control systems.

items.headline: New Gentlemen Ransomware Campaign Targets Critical Infrastructure with Self-Propagation
items.summary: Microsoft identified an emerging ransomware-as-a-service operation called The Gentlemen that combines advanced encryption with self-propagation capabilities specifically targeting critical sectors. The threat group demonstrates sophisticated techniques that could rapidly spread through industrial networks once initial access is gained. Organizations in critical infrastructure should prioritize network segmentation and endpoint detection capabilities to prevent lateral movement.

items.headline: EU Critical Sector Cybersecurity Maturity Shows Improvement But Remains Inconsistent
items.summary: ENISA's NIS360 report found rising cybersecurity maturity across high-criticality sectors in the EU, but progress remains uneven between different industries and member states. The assessment highlights persistent gaps in cybersecurity preparedness that could leave critical infrastructure vulnerable to sophisticated attacks. The findings underscore the need for more standardized security frameworks and accelerated investment in defensive capabilities across essential services.
